samples.summary: New invariant doc ("Callers that write w/h on a rotated frame must go through this") is not true in-tree: the text autogrow path still patches size only
samples.evidence: resize.ts:117-118 asserts "Callers that write `w`/`h` on a rotated frame must go through this (or `resizeFrameWorld`) rather than patching size alone." But editor.ts:4420 still does `store.updateElementFrame(slideId, elementId, { h: targetH })` on a text element that may carry its own non-zero `frame.rotation` (the guard there is only `ancestorHasTransform`, i.e. rotated/scaled *ancestor groups*, not the element's own rotation). That is exactly the #1039 shape of bug — a rotated textbox that auto-grows will drift rather than grow in place. The issue is panel-scoped so this is arguably out of scope, but the change writes a repo-wide rule into a shared module that the repo does not actually satisfy, and the design note in slides-format-options-panel.md §W/H likewise implies the panel was "the one size-changing path that skips it" (todo line 15).
searchedFor: grep updateElementFrame across packages/{slides,frontend}/src with w:/h: patterns
grep onCommitFrame/onLockedResize/commitFrame to find other panel W/H paths

samples.summary: `anchoredFramePatch` is UI-agnostic frame math living in the frontend app layer rather than beside `resizeFrameToSize` in @wafflebase/slides
samples.evidence: frame-patch.ts contains no React/UI concern — it is a two-line `Partial<Frame>` widening of `resizeFrameToSize`. Placing it in packages/frontend/src/app/slides/format-panel/ means any future non-frontend caller (slides' own editor commands, board) must re-derive the same patch-widening. The originating todo (docs/tasks/active/20260907-...-todo.md step 3) explicitly prescribes this location, so it is a taste point, not a violation; the geometry itself is correctly reused rather than duplicated.

samples.summary: New design-doc section does not record how the compensated x/y interacts with the group bake path it sits next to
samples.evidence: The new "W/H on a rotated element" section covers per-element rotation, aspect lock and θ=0 identity, but `commitFrame`/`lockedResize` also run `store.bakeGroupResize` on the same elements in the same batch (index.tsx:131, 244). The doc does not say whether a rotated *group* gets compensated before or after baking, which is the one composition a reader of this section would ask about. Purely a documentation-completeness point; behaviour appears unchanged for groups at θ=0.
